Thermal runaway risk is low (Da_thermal << 0.1) due to the moderate exotherm of SnAr, but pressure management is critical. Both candidates currently have a BPR set to 2.0 bar, which is dangerously inadequate for 120°C DMF (P_vap ~ 0.4-0.5 bar, but safety margins require > 1.5-2.0 bar minimum, and robustness requires higher). Candidate 2 has a massive pressure drop (9.15 bar) which, combined with the low BPR setting, creates a high risk of system overpressure or pump cavitation if the BPR is not raised significantly. Material compatibility is acceptable for PFA at 120°C, but the long coil lengths pose handling risks. The primary safety mandate is to raise the BPR on both candidates to at least 3.0 bar (recommended 4.0 bar for Candidate 2) to ensure safe operation.
